unmapped_findings: The 9Al-20Mn-1C alloy tempered at 800 °C is not covered by any dedicated micrograph in the paper; for this composition/condition only the hardness value (249 HV, Table 8) and the thermodynamic austenite-stability argument (Fig. 12(a)) are reported.

Per the conclusions, tempering at 800 °C in general triggered complete and widespread transformations such as cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition, but for the 9Al-20Mn-1C composition the austenite is more stable at 800 °C than at 1150 °C, so no such transformation was detected — reactions involving the austenite volume at 800 °C were reported only for the 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn-1C grades.

The grain-striation and κ + α (and/or M3C) grain-boundary precipitate observations attributed to 9Al-20Mn-1C (Figs. 10(a) and 11; hardening at 600 °C without detectable austenite transformation, Table 8) pertain to the 600 °C tempered state, NOT to this 800 °C sample, and are therefore not assigned to this sample's structure/property fields.

At 800 °C the CALPHAD equilibrium for 9Al-20Mn-1C gives BCC_A2 = 0 mol (vanishes near 750 °C) and KAPPA_E21 = 0 mol (vanishes by ~800 °C) while FCC_A1 ≈ 1.00 mol, supporting an essentially fully austenitic equilibrium state.
